videos.title: You've been parsing JSON Wrong
videos.author: @devopstoolbox
videos.why: jq tutorial from DevOps Toolbox (136k subscribers, uploaded 2025-10-10) with manual English captions; its worked example (a team JSON file, select by salary, raw output, del of keys) runs offline with jq alone.

s2.task: Using jq, create team.json describing a small startup: an object with "startup", "location" and a "team" array of at least four members, each with "name", "salary" (a number) and "skills" (an array), with at least one salary above 115000 and at least one at or below it. Then, as in the video, write the raw names (no quotes) of the members whose salary is over 115000 to high_earners.txt, one per line, and write the team array with every member's "skills" key deleted to team_no_skills.json.
s2.verify: test -s high_earners.txt && jq -e '(.team | length) >= 4 and (.team | map(.salary > 115000) | any) and (.team | map(.salary <= 115000) | any)' team.json > /dev/null && jq -r '.team[] | select(.salary > 115000) | .name' team.json | diff - high_earners.txt > /dev/null && ! grep -q '"' high_earners.txt && jq -e 'type == "array" and length >= 4 and all(.[]; has("skills") | not)' team_no_skills.json > /dev/null
